title: Chartered Accountant Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Learn how to convert a chartered accountant salary from hourly to annual, including tax, super, and award rates. Use our 38-hour week formula.
salarySummary: The median chartered accountant salary in Australia is around $2,003 per week, or $53 per hour based on a 38-hour week, before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the average chartered accountant salary in Australia?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data from May 2025, the median full-time accountants earn a median weekly earnings of $2,003, which equates to roughly $53 per hour. This figure is a guide and does not account for experience, location, or specialisation. For award-covered accountants, minimum rates may apply under the Professional Employees Award, but many chartered accountants are above award.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary for a chartered accountant?
faqs.a: Use the formula: annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a standard 38-hour week, multiply your hourly rate by 1,976 (38 × 52). For example, at $53 per hour, annual gross is about $104,728. A fortnightly amount is simply the weekly figure multiplied by 2. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What tax and super should I expect on a chartered accountant salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates apply: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830. Use our take-home pay calculator for an estimate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the chartered accountant salary landscape

When evaluating a **chartered accountant salary**, it's essential to understand how hourly rates translate to annual income, especially if you are considering a contract role or comparing offers. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that the median full-time earnings for accountants (which includes chartered accountants) is $2,003 per week, or $53 per hour, based on a 38-hour week. However, actual hours worked can be higher—the average full-time accountant works 43 hours per week—so your annual figure may differ if you work more than the standard 38 hours.

### How to convert hourly rates to annual salary

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38-hour week unless stated otherwise. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44. For a chartered accountant earning $53 per hour, the annual gross would be $53 × 38 × 52 = $104,728. The fortnightly amount is simply the weekly figure multiplied by two: $2,003 per week becomes $4,006 per fortnight.

This conversion assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. If you work more than 38 hours regularly, your actual annual income will be higher. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to calculate your own figures.

### The role of awards and the National Minimum Wage

Not all chartered accountants are covered by an award, but understanding the minimum wage framework is useful. The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the National Minimum Wage at $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week from 1 July 2026. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from the same date. For example, the Clerks—Private Sector Award 2020 sets minimum rates for clerical workers, but accountants are typically covered by the Professional Employees Award, which has higher minimum rates. Casual employees receive a 25% casual loading on top of the minimum hourly rate, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. If you are a casual chartered accountant, your hourly rate should include this loading—never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; instead, use our [casual loading calculator to add it.

### Tax and superannuation on your chartered accountant salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate tax and super. For 2026–27 resident tax rates, the first $18,200 is tax-free, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,000 maximum contribution base. For a chartered accountant earning $104,728, the tax estimate would be approximately $22,000 plus Medicare, leaving a take-home pay of around $80,000. Use our [take-home pay calculator for a more detailed breakdown.

### Important considerations and limitations

Our conversion uses a 38-hour week, but many accountants work 43 hours per week. If you work 43 hours, multiply by 43 instead. The ABS data shows median hourly earnings for accountants is $53, but that includes all experience levels. Your actual chartered accountant salary may be higher or lower. Always check the relevant award or enterprise agreement if applicable. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed pay rates, see our [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).
